scan_notes: Reviewed the full scoped diff, emphasizing the round-8 changes and both page directories. The round-7 recompute-completeness issue is closed: scenario components and both control docks are now reconciled against each response. The caveat’s struck/current pairing is unambiguous, the seven red-team paragraph escapes are corrected, and no resolver/renderer disagreement was found in the as-of mechanism. The fact-check passed; 134 targeted Python tests passed, with one additional test blocked because the read-only environment could not create tmp_path. Vitest and fresh browser inspection were likewise blocked by the read-only sandbox. The chart findings below are nevertheless established directly by the tracked builder declarations and renderer branches, not inferred from an unmeasured screenshot.

findings.title: Simulator turns a hidden band edge into a visible series
findings.evidence: The authored specification recreates the upper edge as `{ mark: 'line' ... }` and the lower edge as `{ mark: 'area' ... fill_to: 'previous' }`. The source builder declares both corresponding traces with `line=dict(width=0)` and hides the upper trace from the legend (`api/services/smp/loan_simulator.py:327-331`). `ChartView.tsx:1972-2005,2098-2115` draws the fill without a stroke but then draws the area trace’s Line, while the partner is also rendered as a normal Line. The README declares only the changed fill colour.
findings.failure_scenario: Whenever cohort dispersion contains at least three observations, the ordinary initial payload or a recompute includes `sim-dispersion`. The published authored page shows boundary curves around the ±1σ region, including a full-strength `+1 std` curve and its extra legend entry; the builder-served Plotly chart shows a fill with those boundary traces at zero width and suppresses the upper legend entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Represent and preserve `line.width: 0` and `showlegend: false` through the chart contract/compiler/renderer, then set them on these two authored series. If that fidelity cannot be implemented, declare both visible differences in the README.

findings.title: Forecast draws outlines for ten width-zero band traces
findings.evidence: The book band is emitted as a normal partner line plus an area at lines 205-207, and the same pair is repeated four times at lines 247-262. The builder sets all ten corresponding traces to `line=dict(width=0)` (`api/services/smp/forecast.py:1001-1006,1202-1205`). The authored `mk()` allowlist carries neither width nor a no-stroke flag, and `ChartView.tsx` renders both the partner and filled series as Lines in addition to the unstroked fill. The README’s complete difference list discusses legend rows but does not disclose these new outlines.
findings.failure_scenario: On every normal forecast page load, the existing-book band and all four new-cohort bands are present. Readers see five uncertainty regions framed by added boundary curves, whereas the builder-served page intentionally renders all ten edges at zero width. This makes the regions look more crisply bounded than the source presentation.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a supported no-stroke or zero-width series property and carry it for these ten traces. Also update the README’s difference list if any unavoidable visual divergence remains.

findings.title: Forecast README undercounts extra band legend rows
findings.evidence: The README says `Eight band traces` and attributes only `6` to `new-milestone-fig`. The tracked figure has four products with two hidden band traces each, so that figure contributes eight extra legend rows itself. Together with one hidden trace in `book-milestone-fig` and one in `runoff-fig`, the authored page adds ten rows.
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer compares the published authored page with the builder-served page. They see ten additional minted legend entries, while the supposedly complete reader-visible difference list tells them to expect eight and omits two from the new-cohort chart.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the heading and breakdown to ten total: runoff 1, book milestone 1, and new milestone 8.

findings.title: Forecast README identifies the wrong built artifact
findings.evidence: The README claims `BUILD_BASE 136d7a98` and `1,172,300 bytes`. The tracked `build_base.txt` contains `dd45836e4e14b7ac1b183bd048859590dcca4d9d`, and the tracked `build/out.html` is 1,172,594 bytes.
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer uses the README’s gate record to identify or reproduce the artifact. They select the old base and byte count instead of the artifact currently committed beside the README, so the record does not establish which bytes received the listed checks.
findings.suggested_fix: Refresh both values from `build_base.txt` and `wc -c build/out.html`, preferably with a guard that compares the README against those files.

findings.title: Caveat guard enforces current wording only corpus-wide
findings.evidence: The test builds one corpus-wide `unstruck` list and asserts only that it is nonempty: `for readme in _readmes() ... if quoted == current and not struck`. It does not require each README containing historical caveat quotes to also quote the current emitted wording.
findings.failure_scenario: Another authored README contains only a struck copy of an older caveat. The stale-quote test accepts it because it is struck, and this symmetric test still passes because `smp_simulator/README.md` supplies a current quote elsewhere. Readers of the new README receive no statement of the wording its rebuild would render.
findings.suggested_fix: Group quotes by README and require an unstruck current quote in every README that contains any recognized caveat quote.

overall_explanation: No high-severity defect was found, so the round-7 recompute-completeness question is closed and the terminal-round stopping condition is met. Two deterministic, undeclared chart-fidelity defects remain: both pages render outlines that their builders explicitly suppress. The remaining findings concern inaccurate build/difference documentation and a non-per-page caveat regression guard.
